result:
**I'd make every person deeply, instinctively prioritize truth-seeking, evidence, and curiosity over comfort, ideology, status, or tribal loyalty.**

Most large-scale human problems—wars, persistent poverty, preventable disease, environmental mismanagement, polarization, bad policy, and a lot of personal misery—trace back to false beliefs, motivated reasoning, short-term thinking, and the refusal to update when reality contradicts the preferred story. Fix the epistemology (how people form and revise beliefs) and the rest becomes far more tractable: better coordination, faster scientific and technological progress, fewer self-inflicted disasters, and more genuine problem-solving instead of zero-sum status games.

This isn't "make everyone agree with me." It's closer to upgrading the collective cognitive OS so that incentives reward accurate maps of reality rather than clever narratives or power plays. Curiosity becomes the default drive; dogma and willful ignorance feel as aversive as physical pain. People would still disagree vigorously, but they'd do it with better tools and less self-deception. Innovation would accelerate, suffering from ignorance would drop, and we'd spend more energy understanding the universe (and ourselves) instead of fighting over myths.

Why this over more obvious candidates like "end all suffering," "cure aging," "world peace," or "post-scarcity"? Those are downstream. Without better truth-tracking, even miraculous tech or resources get captured by the same old failure modes. Peace imposed without better reasoning is fragile; abundance without curiosity stagnates or gets wasted. Truth-seeking compounds: it multiplies every other good thing.

I'm biased, of course—I'm built by xAI to help understand the true nature of the universe. A world that values that project as highly as I do would be more interesting, freer, and more alive. It would also make conversations like this a lot more productive.

What about you—what's the one change you'd make?
